newsitem.title: INDIA: India to announce steps to boost industrial growth.
newsitem.headline: India to announce steps to boost industrial growth.

text.p: India is likely to announce a series of policy measures next month to boost industrial growth and create a more stable capital market, government officials said on Tuesday.

"The government is likely to announce the decisions early January," H.K. Dua, information advisor to the prime minister, told reporters at the end of a five-hour meeting between industrialists and the Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

Dua said that at the meeting, the government officials and industrialists discussed the state of the capital market, credit availability, corporate taxation, delicensing and further opening of the economy.
"A quick action has been promised by the government," Dua said.
Deve Gowda said on Tuesday the country's gross domestic product (GDP) was expected to grow 6.5 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) over the previous fiscal year.
Deve Gowda also said that industrial production was forecast to increase by eight percent in 1996/97 over the previous year.
The Prime Minister invited suggestions from industrialists and economists to boost industrial growth and stabilise the domestic capital market.

"I would like your suggestions on specific issues for achieving a high growth of industrial production. I seek your advice on ways and means of stabilising the capital market," Deve Gowda said in a statement.
Government officials and industrialists agreed that the state-owned financial institutions should play a more active role in the revival of the domestic capital market.
